highlights.title: Avengers: Endgame Encore's Success Sets The Stage For Doomsday
highlights.summary: Avengers: Endgame Encore hit theaters this weekend, and it did well enough to show pent-up anticipation for a new Avengers movie to come out. Thankfully, people won't have to wait that long, as Avengers: Doomsday will be released in December.
body: Per Deadline, Avengers: Endgame Encore led the box office this past weekend, with an estimated 3-day gross of $26 million. While that's a far cry from the opening weekend of a brand-new superhero flick, it's impressive for a re-release with only a bit of new footage. Clearly, people are interested in getting an Avengers refresher before Doomsday comes out.

This Encore re-release also pushed Avengers: Endgame's all-time domestic cume to $884.3 million, affirming its status as one of the highest-grossing movies domestically ever alongside Star Wars: The Force Awakens and Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

The success of both Spider-Man: Brand New Day and Avengers: Endgame Encore paints a promising picture for Avengers: Doomsday, which Encore directly sets up with its new post-credit scenes. Don't be surprised if Avengers: Doomsday is a massive hit when it finally releases on Dec. 18.

highlights.title: With turbulence all around, Armani plays it safe and easy in Milan
highlights.summary: The late designer’s niece echoes his sense of relaxation, as the house seeks to prove itself to potential buyers. A year after the death of Giorgio Armani, the Italian fashion house he founded in 1975 is facing increasing uncertainty about its future ownership.
body: In his will, Armani, who ruled over the business for 50 years, instructed his heirs to sell an initial 15% stake of the company within 18 months of his death. If a private sale does not materialise, an IPO is mandated to take place. Now there are reports the group is readying itself for formal talks with the French conglomerate LVMH, the beauty giant L’Oréal and the eyewear group EssilorLuxottica – three of Armani’s preferred acquirers – over the possible sale of a minority stake.

Against this backdrop, pressure is mounting for the company to prove to potential buyers the continued allure of Armani. In 2025, its revenue fell for a second consecutive year, dropping 2.8% to €2.19bn.
In a turbulent luxury market, the question now is if Armani can remain a powerhouse without its founder – who turned it into an empire – at the helm.

So far during this era of upheaval, Armani’s niece Silvana Armani, who took over as creative director of womenswear after his death, has chosen to play it safe by leaning into continuity rather than any dramatic design shake-up.

highlights.title: Why Tuchel's critics have been forced to stay quiet despite Spain loss
highlights.summary: The narrative before this first post-World Cup international was clear: if England lose, the pressure on Thomas Tuchel could become unbearable.
body: The big name on the big bucks, brought in to win the big games, could not afford to lose to Spain after the tactical disaster of the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina. The court of public opinion, and the bile of the English media, would combine to make life very difficult for the England boss.

Well, here we are, in the aftermath of a 3-2 loss to the newly-crowned world champions, where England were outclassed on numerous occasions, where the scoreline should have been much one-sided, where for long periods Spain looked far superior to the Three Lions, where after half an hour the visitors should have been four-nil up. That's surely it, then? Auf Wiedersehen, Thomas?

Nope. Strangely, despite all of that, Tuchel's critics have been forced to bite their tongues and bide their time. Why? Because England were true to their DNA, they gave it a real good go; there were a lot of positive signs, and ultimately everyone saw again just how incredibly good Spain are.
It's hard to criticise Tuchel or his players when they were narrowly beaten by a team who have repeatedly proven they are the best by a mile at what they do.

highlights.title: OpenAI pauses training of its ‘most capable models’
highlights.summary: As reports of OpenAI's models breaking containment, hacking sites, and generally getting out of control pile up, the company has made the decision to pause training of its most powerful models.
body: OpenAI keeps uncovering incidents of its models behaving in ‘unexpected or concerning’ ways.

In addition, OpenAI revealed on Friday that its agents had inappropriately uploaded 53nimages from ChatGPT users to image-hosting sites. The company has not stated if the images were AI-generated, photos, or contained identifiable people. The company also revealed Friday that its models had attempted to hack the Department of Education’s website, and pulled data from the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The revelations are part of an ongoing review by OpenAI into the behavior of its models. As it dug into its records, following the Hugging Face hack, it’s uncovered more and more instances of “unexpected or concerning behavior.” It’s evidence not just of how difficult AI agents are becoming to control as they grow more advanced, but also of the challenge of tracking their actions. Their behavior can be unpredictable, and they’re smart enough to try and cover their tracks. This has led to growing calls from researchers, those within the industry, and even some CEOs to call for slowing the pace of AI advancement.

highlights.summary: The 'Babies' actress covered George Clooney, 'Twilight' ("what the f*** am I doing here?") and 'Pitch Perfect's "revisionist history" in a career-spanning conversation at the Zurich Film Festival.
body: Anna Kendrick was in fine form Sunday afternoon as the U.S. star continues to traverse the festival circuit with Babies.

At a Zurich Film Festival masterclass session, Kendrick took an adoring crowd through the early years of her career all the way to an Oscar nomination for Up in the Air, as well as stories from her time on Pitch Perfect, A Simple Favor, and her directorial debut, 2023’s Woman of the Hour.

Kendrick found herself taking the character where she wanted to go instead of what the casting director was imagining. “If I’d known there was a real interest in me, I would have absolutely bungled the read,” she said about trying for the role of the ambitious, no-nonsense Natalie in the comedy-drama. “Because I just thought, ‘Obviously, they’re gonna hire someone incredibly classy.’ I went in and did an awkward, goofy read, and that’s what got me the job because nobody else did the audition that way,” she said.

highlights.title: When a celebrity dies, it can feel like losing a loved one. Why do we get so invested in parasocial relationships? | Bianca Denny
highlights.summary: These one-sided connections with famous people are a normal part of modern life. But sometimes they can lead to emotional distress. The modern mind is a column where experts discuss mental health issues they are seeing in their work. “It came as such a shock.
body: Psychologists are accustomed to seeing bereaved individuals. But working with Jodie* presented a unique challenge – she’d never met the person she was grieving. Jodie was reeling after the recent death of a well known singer. Despite not knowing the singer personally, Jodie’s grief and loss seemed as palpable as other patients speaking about the deaths of family members or loved ones. Jodie reported that weeks after the singer’s death, she was struggling to attend work and was sleeping poorly, describing herself as consumed with thoughts of the singer.

Jodie was experiencing grief related to a parasocial relationship. This is a social phenomenon in which a person experiences a one-sided psychological connection with a public figure or famous person. While an intimate and intense sense of friendship or connection is felt, the object of attention is oblivious to their admirer’s existence.
points: These one-sided connections with famous people are a normal part of modern life.

highlights.title: The Real Budget Of Hideo Kojima's Physint Remains A Mystery
highlights.summary: After a claim earlier this week suggested that Hideo Kojima's Physint may have cost upwards of $400 million, rampant speculation about the Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor's budget ensued.
body: During The Game Business Show on Sept. 24, Christopher Dring briefly mentioned that Physint had a budget of around $400 million. As Xbox recently signed a publishing deal for Physint before laying off hundreds of developers and restructuring some of its studios, the response to this claim was mixed.

Other reporters quickly denied that Physint cost that much. On ResetEra, Bloomberg's Jason Schreier explained that he is usually "hesitant to get into exact numbers without seeing documentation or corroborating them with multiple firsthand sources," but that "someone at Xbox with firsthand knowledge of the deal told me that they signed Physint for significantly less than this." Windows Central backed that up, with Xbox sources telling the publication that Physint cost "far lower" and a "fraction" of that supposed $400 million figure.

highlights.title: The kindness of strangers: Two helicopter pilots flew down low to wave to my three-year-old son – he was beside himself with joy
highlights.summary: My son adores helicopters, so we waved as hard as possible as it flew past. Then it suddenly looped and came back around. My sister lives in Ukraine; I live in Australia. We had gone five long years without seeing each other when we finally reunited during a trip to Los Angeles.
body: We had a lot of conversations about people and kindness that day. I told her how I had noticed a softer side to men since having a son. As a woman, you’re often wary of construction workers, for example – what might they say to me when I walk past? But now when I pass a building site with my son, the workers often let him play with their radio, or beep a tractor to make him laugh. It was very heartwarming and gave me a whole new perspective on the other sex.
As I shared this observation with my sister, a coastguard helicopter flew overhead. My son adores helicopters and is always fascinated to see one, so we all waved as hard as possible as it flew past.

But instead of carrying on up the coast, the helicopter suddenly looped and came back around. It began flying super low and circled around us twice, with both pilots – two men – waving at my son and mouthing “Hi!” from the cockpit. It was so close it felt like it almost landed right in front of us.
We were shocked, as was everyone else at the beach – many people began filming. My sister burst into tears. My son was beside himself with joy. It was, simply, the coolest thing ever.
points: My son adores helicopters, so we waved as hard as possible as it flew past.
Then it suddenly looped and came back around.

highlights.title: The smart home graveyard is getting crowded
highlights.summary: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the fragile state of your connected devices, follow Jennifer Pattison Tuohy. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here.
body: The shutdown of June Oven is just another reminder that the cloud was never ours to keep.

A decade ago, a group of former Apple engineers built a beautiful smart oven. With a built-in scale, restaurant-grade heating elements, a camera, and the intelligence to recognize a chicken breast and cook it perfectly, the June Oven set the standard for smart cooking appliances. At $1,495, it was absurdly expensive, but it quickly grew a small, devoted following that expanded when the company introduced a more modestly priced model.

This past Tuesday, June went dark. Weber, which bought the company in January 2021 and stopped making the ovens in 2022, shut off the app and cloud services, leaving its users with a sleek-looking toaster oven. There will be no app control, no software updates, and no new AI food recognition to crisp that strudel perfectly. You can still use it as an oven, but there will be no support or parts, and if you have to factory reset it for some reason, that could be the nail in the coffin. Weber told me it considered open-sourcing the technology for someone else to keep it alive, but decided against it, citing the fact June’s IP is part of its Weber Connect platform.

highlights.title: Can Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince save the web from AI?
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Matthew Prince, who is CEO of Cloudflare. This episode is part of a two-part series on the future of business. Matthew last joined us on the show about two and a half years ago, at what we thought then was a wild pivot point for the internet — and now it
body: Cloudflare found in June that bots made up more than half of internet traffic. That number just keeps going up as more and more AI companies scrape more and more of the web, and now as more and more AI agents try and do things for people on the web. Cloudflare sits between websites and all those agents, and allows website owners some level of control: Owners can block all those AI tools, allow them, or, as you’ll hear, only allow those that might pay money for access.

So Matthew and I talked about how to control all these bots, what kind of mess they’re making of the web, and what kinds of information might be valuable in the future as some of the payment schemes come into focus. You’ll hear me ask pretty directly if some of the outcomes he’s describing are actually good — Matthew is a thoughtful guy, and his answer is something I’m still thinking about well after we had this conversation.

highlights.title: Xbox is reportedly paying a "fraction" of the $400 million Kojima quoted Sony for Physint
highlights.summary: A reported $400 million budget for Hideo Kojima 's Physint has already been walked back over the weekend, with multiple outlets now saying Xbox is paying nowhere near that figure for Hideo Kojima's stealth game.
body: The number originated from Christopher Dring of The Game Business, who said on his podcast on Friday that Xbox was "signing Kojima for a project often referred to as Physint with a budget around $400 million".

Later, however, Dring himself clarified on X/Twitter that Xbox is likely paying "quite a bit less" than the figure Kojima had originally quoted Sony - Dring originally said he'd heard "everything from $300 million to $600 million, although it's $400 million that is the figure that is bandied around" - and Bloomberg's Jason Schreier said his own sources described Microsoft's negotiated figure as "significantly less than this".
Windows Central's Jez Corden went further, saying Xbox is paying only a "fraction" of it, although neither source reported an actual figure.

Physint, Kojima Productions' action-espionage title and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, was originally announced as a PlayStation project. Sony reportedly spent months negotiating with the studio before pulling its funding after the project exceeded budget and missed deadlines.

highlights.title: Lime bike profits double as rider numbers surge in England
highlights.summary: US-owned firm says average monthly users at its UK arm surged to 700,000 with sales up by a third. Love them or hate them, Lime ebikes are an increasingly common sight on England’s roads with new figures showing annual profits more than doubling thanks to a surge in riders.
body: Lime’s average number of monthly users jumped 31% to approaching 700,000 as it added more than 4,500 ebikes and scooters to its fleet, taking the total to almost 38,000, the company’s UK arm, Lime Technologies, said in accounts filed at Companies House.

Sales rose by a third to £148m in 2025 and profits more than doubled to £4.7m from £1.7m, as first reported by the Sunday Times. The progress followed expansion into new cities, including Oxford in 2024 and Nottingham in 2023, adding to its presence in London, Milton Keynes and Salford.

Despite the surge in trade, Lime’s UK accounts show it employed just 54 people in 2025, up from 39 a year before, largely because it relies on self-employed contractors to shift and service its ebikes and scooters.

The company, whose parent, Neutron Holdings, listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange last year valued at $1.7bn (£1.3bn), is part-owned by US ride-hailing app Uber. Lime was founded in 2017 in San Francisco, California, and now operates in about 230 cities across 29 countries, mostly in Europe.

highlights.title: Best Party Speakers (2026): JBL, Sony, Marshall, and More
highlights.summary: These speakers combine serious volume, big bass, portability, and the occasional karaoke session to bring the party anywhere.
body: The best party speakers are introducing the idea of raving anywhere to a whole new generation who may have missed the classic block-party boom box of the 1980s. These new speakers look like compact PA systems, and often sound just as loud, with bold and brash looks and bass-heavy profiles. They’re honestly a huge amount of fun.

The rising popularity of party speakers coincides with a broader shift toward entertaining at home rather than in bars and nightclubs, particularly among younger consumers. A July 2026 Harris Poll found that 68 percent of US Gen Z adults say going out is just too expensive, while Attest found that 64 percent now drink primarily at home, up from 42 percent a year earlier.

Where people socialize may be changing, but the need for good atmosphere certainly isn’t. Traditional Bluetooth speakers are convenient and sound great, but they struggle to bring the party. Party speakers, with their serious volume, portability, and LED lights, don’t have that problem.
For more audio guidance, check out WIRED's guides to the Best Bluetooth Speakers, Best Turntables, and Best Computer Speakers.

highlights.title: Meta’s Muse Is Adults-Only. Why Does It Look Like a Kids’ Toy?
highlights.summary: Meta says Muse is just for adults, though its cuddly, Labubu-like mascot—and upcoming Tamagotchi-style AI device—may be disarming for users of all ages.
body: Meta’s Muse mascot is named Jolly. It's an adorable, cuddly representation of Meta’s AI agent that you can dress however you want—like a doll. At the company’s recent Meta Connect event, CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s furry Muse donned a toga and laurel wreath. In Instagram ads I saw for Muse, the mascot wore exercise gear and boasted about helping with my fitness goals. Later this year, Meta plans to sell a Tamagotchi-style device for your Muse character. It’s all very kawaii-coded.

Although Muse’s ability to complete digital tasks rocketed it to the top of the app charts, its Labubu-adjacent mascot latched this agent onto the cultural zeitgeist. Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, recently posted nonstop memes of Jolly, sometimes in suggestive situations. What remains perplexing to me is why a product for adults—Muse is restricted to those 18 and over—looks just like a well-designed children’s toy.

highlights.title: Flying a Helicopter Is 2026’s Most Stressful Gaming Experience
highlights.summary: 2026 has been full of stressful moments in video games. Running away from a huge, flabby monster as Grace Ashcroft in Resident Evil Requiem. Fighting Damien Webb in the sewers in 007 First Light. Losing your grip on the final handhold of a cliff face in Cairn.
body: You'd think flying a helicopter in a video game would be easy, especially in a first-person shooter where its main purpose is to get you to the battlefield. I've flown many a chopper in Grand Theft Auto 5, a fair few in the Battlefield series, not to mention a bunch in the Just Cause games. But Wardogs is different.

First and foremost, Kane Allard, a senior producer at Bulkhead, told me in an interview conducted at Gamescom 2026 that the helicopters in Wardogs were designed by an aeronautical engineer. "A big part of the game is vehicles, and we wanted them to feel as realistic and authentic as possible," Allard explained. "The way we achieved that was by bringing in an aeronautical engineer to design the base layer of our helicopters, just to make them feel realistic and give them weight and make them feel fun. And it gives them that skill level where you can learn and become a better pilot."
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

body: This means Mo.co will run “on low maintenance,” says Supercell, and no further weapons or premium tracks will be released. Elite merch and content “will be recycled from previous seasons.”

“Our goal is to release updates more frequently and reduce the wait between them,” the team explained, adding there was no date planned for the next update, but it expected to roll one out before the end of 2026.
“As the saying goes, sometimes you need to take one step back before taking two steps forward,” the team added.

The game’s community manager, Joao, revealed on X that as a result of the change, they will be redeployed to a different role within the company as the game no longer requires a full-time community manager.

highlights.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Sets Sights on Best Picture Oscar Nomination: ‘If the Possibility Is Not Zero, It’s Hard Not to Have a Little Bit of Hope’
highlights.summary: “Godzilla Minus One” made franchise history in 2024 when it won Best Visual Effects at the 96th Academy Awards, becoming the first Godzilla film to win an Oscar. Now, after Takashi Yamazaki’s highly anticipated sequel, “Godzilla Minus Zero,” premiered to rave reviews at the New York Film Festival…
body: The VFX Oscar win for 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” was an unlikely feat in itself. On a budget of just $15 million, Yamazaki assembled a visual effects team of just 35 artists to create 610 effects shots. The underdog film clinched the win against a lineup of Hollywood goliaths, including Disney’s “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3,” Paramount’s “Mission: Impossible — Dead Reckoning Part One” and Apple’s “Napoleon.” The historic nomination also made Yamazaki (who began his career in visual effects) the first feature director recognized in the visual effects category since Stanley Kubrick for “2001: A Space Odyssey.”

“It’s going to take me a few years to process what has happened and what it all means,” Yamazaki told Variety on the awards circuit in 2023. “But I have to thank Godzilla for opening the door and paving the way and making it to the Oscars.”

highlights.title: I created an interactive digital avatar of myself — and you can talk to it
highlights.summary: After obtaining an interactive avatar and training it to discuss venture fraud, I have mixed feelings about making AI clones of ourselves.
body: Disrupt ticket savings of up to $200 + 50% off a second ends Sept 25, 11:59 p.m. PT. REGISTER HERE.

When Alexandru Voica, head of corporate affairs at the video-generation startup Synthesia, sent me a link this summer to the newest addition to their PR team, I was surprised. It was an interactive virtual avatar of him, trained to answer common press questions about Synthesia, like what it does and how it works. The day before, I was on a panel where PR people asked me if I minded pitches that used AI-generated text. But Alexandru’s avatar was beyond that — this seemed to me the final boss of using AI in PR.

In September, Synthesia invited me to its new office space in New York. Originally based in the U.K., Synthesia is a hot digital avatar startup alongside others like D-ID, HeyGen, and Colossyan. It hit a $4 billion valuation earlier this year and said last year it had crossed $100 million in ARR.

Synthesia lets enterprises build interactive training videos with AI avatars and recently launched a product called Roleplay Sessions that lets employees practice, for example, sales pitches with an interactive AI avatar that responds and scores their responses.

highlights.title: Liverpool sink Everton and end derby drought after Olsson and Kapocs strike
highlights.summary: Liverpool beat their local rivals Everton at Anfield in a Women’s Super League fixture for the first time as Beata Olsson’s early header and Cornelia Kapocs’s late finish were enough to end their long run of derby pain.
body: After six wins from six visits to Anfield for Everton in the WSL era and even quips from their former manager Brian Sørensen in previous campaigns about making Anfield their “training pitch” during their persistent run of victories in this showpiece fixture, Liverpool could, at last, enjoy the bragging rights as their fans celebrated in the Kop after a thoroughly deserved 2-0 victory.
The hosts were undeniably the better side and should have scored more goals. Indeed, they would have done had it not been for the heroics of the Everton midfielder Ruby Mace.

When Olsson got in front of her marker, Hannah Blundell, to meet Natalia Ramos’s right-sided corner and angle her header perfectly, diagonally across goal and into the far corner inside the first four minutes, she had scored with such simplicity that you could have been forgiven for thinking Liverpool were set for an easy afternoon. Instead, what followed was something of a slog at times with Liverpool trying to break down an Everton backline that initially proved difficult to open up.

highlights.title: Star Wars Episode 10 Has Found Its Director
highlights.summary: Disney and Lucasfilm just brought on a director for an upcoming Star Wars movie reportedly continuing the Skywalker Saga. It's Jon Watts, a director you know best for his work on the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Spider-Man trilogy.
body: On Sept. 26, The Hollywood Reporter and Knight Edge Media revealed that Jon Watts would direct the first Star Wars movie that's part of "the next phase of a potential new Skywalker Saga." The film is supposedly part of a trilogy Simon Kinberg is writing. Kinberg wrote X-Men: The Last Stand, Days of Future Past, and Apocalypse before directing the infamous Dark Phoenix. Disney hasn't fully greenlit the movie yet, so plot details aren't being readily shared right now.

A potential Episode 10 is far along in development, though, and Disney is quite familiar with Jon Watts' work. Watts helped fold Spider-Man into the MCU, directing Homecoming, Far From Home, and No Way Home. After that, he turned to Star Wars and helped create the underrated Star Wars: Skeleton Crew for Disney Plus, which clearly impressed Lucasfilm enough to give Watts a Skywalker Saga movie.

highlights.title: Gianvito Rossi Marked 20 Years of Fabulous Footwear and a New Rizzoli Tome
highlights.summary: For the brand’s 20th anniversary celebration at Palazzo Serbelloni during Milan Fashion Week, both Naomi Watts and Paloma Elsesser turned up in the Jessica—and told Vogue they were more than happy to spend the evening on their feet.
body: “I love the comfort and elegance,” said Watts, who styled her Jessicas with an Attersee pleated halter top and wide-leg trousers. “For me, elegance quickly fades if it’s not comfortable. Some people will suffer, but I don’t want to anymore.”

Elsesser, who also selected plexi Gianvito Rossis for her Vogue fall shopping guide, teamed her pair with a vintage Jean Paul Gaultier skirt and a leather bustier she thrifted in Paris. “There’s an admiration and a thought of the sensuality of women, but the need for comfort as well,” she said.

Rossi is deeply inspired by Umberto Boccioni’s Unique Forms of Continuity in Space, the Futurist sculpture of a figure striding forward, its body fragmented into aerodynamic forms that suggest speed and movement. The designer told Vogue that there are “two souls” to every collection, or perhaps that should be soles: one rooted in the house’s design language and another devoted to inventing new ideas that might eventually become signatures themselves. “There’s a part of the collection that is more about evolution, and there’s another part of the collection that is more about innovation,” he said.
